title: Land the candidate's create/copy/start docker argv and the stdin tar archive (leaf)
description:
LEAF spun out of task-f4f45c281ab64f6dbf2c4ff163140010 (remote deploy cannot deliver environment variables) by architect-ed42e60a, 2026-09-09. That row is the CONSUMER and declares this row in its dependsOn. Filed separately because the consumer's blast radius was measured at 12 files, over the plan cap.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Remote delivery needs the plaintext to reach the container without ever naming a path on the docker host, because a bind mount's source is resolved on the DOCKER host and for sshTarget !== null that is not the daemon's machine. The measured shape is `docker create` + `docker cp -` (a USTAR archive on stdin) + `docker start`: the bytes go host memory -> docker CLI stdin -> container filesystem, and it works identically local and remote because the runner already carries stdin through `ssh <target> docker ...`.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a, not taken from prose:
- `DockerRunner` is `(args, stdin?) => Promise<DeployRunResult>` at deploy-ports.ts:24, and `runProcess` at :153-177 writes that stdin into the child and ends it. `nodeSshRunner` at :184-185 passes it through. So `docker cp -` needs NO new port and NO new capability.
- deploy-service.ts:190-192 already threads stdin through the one `run(target, args, stdin?)` seam for both local and ssh.
- `runCandidateArgv` (deploy-candidate-environment.ts:93-100) is the only builder of the candidate's start argv; `startCandidate` at deploy-service.ts:226-232 is the only caller.
- The docker double's dispatch is deploy-ports.ts:338-370, `if (verb === "run")` at :346 (the parent description said :341 - drift, re-measure).
- `tests/e2e/control-room/fake-docker-dependencies.ts:42` keys candidate health seeding on `args[0] === "run"`.
- No reusable tar writer exists in this repo. `tools/packaging/pack-source.test.ts` is the only USTAR mention and it is a reader-side assertion, not a writer.

SCOPE: BUILDERS AND DOUBLES ONLY. This row wires NOTHING into deploy-service.ts and removes NO refusal. `runCandidateArgv` stays exported and byte-identical, `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` stays in place and still fires for sshTarget !== null, and every existing consumer of the `run` verb stays green WITHOUT EDITS. That is what keeps this row small and its successor reviewable; the successor owns the verb migration and the nine-plus consumer edits.

PUT THE ARCHIVE ENCODER IN ITS OWN FILE. deploy-candidate-environment.ts is already 217 lines and a USTAR writer in this repo's comment density would push it past the 250-line target.

ONE THING THE IMPLEMENTER MUST MEASURE RATHER THAN ASSUME: what `docker cp - <container>:<dest>` does when `dest` does not exist in the image. Copying to `/` with the archive carrying `run/moe/env` plus its directory entries is the shape that cannot fail on a missing destination, but confirm it against a real container before pinning it. The docker daemon was DOWN on this host at filing time; the owner is bringing it up.
definitionOfDone: deploy-candidate-environment.ts exports createCandidateArgv, startCandidateArgv and copyEnvironmentArgv for the candidate, and runCandidateArgv is UNCHANGED - an exact toEqual arm pins both its mount-null and mount-present arms to the same bytes they produce at HEAD today, so the successor row's migration starts from a proven baseline.

A new apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.ts encodes a single-file USTAR archive from the encoded environment text. Arms assert the 512-byte block structure, that the header checksum field validates against a recomputed checksum, that the two trailing zero blocks are present, and that the variable VALUE appears only in the data block and in no header field. Verify the encoder against a real `tar -t`/`docker cp` read-back, not only against its own decoder.

The docker double in deploy-ports.ts answers `create`, `cp` and `start` and tracks container state across create-then-start the way it tracks `run` today, keyed on the `--name` VALUE and not the trailing argv. An arm proves a container that was CREATED but not STARTED does not report itself running, and that `cp` to an absent container refuses rather than succeeding silently.
tests/e2e/control-room/fake-docker-dependencies.ts seeds candidate health for a candidate started by create-then-start as well as by run, with no behaviour change for the run path.

NOTHING IS WIRED: `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` is EMPTY at completion, DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED still exists and resolveCandidateMount still returns it for sshTarget !== null, and every pre-existing arm that pins the `run` verb passes WITHOUT being edited - name them in the record as evidence the baseline was not disturbed.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim, plus pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck EXIT 0. An exit-0 leg with no count line is not a pass.

implementationPlan.description: PRE-FLIGHT, and ONE measurement decides whether the whole design works. Read comment-090db6b7c8d74fe49a90b053a9706571 (architect-978f68c6's measurements) first; I have verified both of its load-bearing findings and this plan is built on them. (1) Bring Docker up and record `docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'`. (2) THE OWNERSHIP PROBE, which is the reason this step exists: `deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:91` emits `USER node`, so the deployed app does NOT run as root, while `docker cp` by default gives copied files ROOT ownership. A mode-0600 root-owned `/run/moe/env` copies successfully and is then UNREADABLE by the process that needs it — which surfaces later as a 150s health timeout with no hint of the cause, the exact failure this whole design exists to avoid. Measure, do not infer: build or pull `node:24.16.0-alpine`, read the app user's real uid and gid (`docker run --rm <image> id -u node` and `id -g node`), then create a container, `docker cp -` an archive in, and read the file back AS THAT USER (`docker exec --user node <c> cat /run/moe/env`). Determine whether ownership comes from the USTAR header's uid/gid fields, whether `docker cp --archive/-a` is required to honour them, and what the destination path must be for a directory that does not exist in the image. DO NOT solve unreadability by running as root or by widening the mode to world-readable — the file holds the environment. Record the measured uid, gid, the exact cp invocation and the successful read-back in the step note; every later step pins these values. (3) Re-census: `wc -l apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ports.ts` (measured 399 — the split in step 2 exists because of this), and confirm `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/deployment tests/e2e/control-room` shows no foreign dirt on the owned paths. Baseline to beat: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --config package.json --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=30000 src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.test.ts` was EXIT 0 with `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 23 passed (23)`.

Split the docker double out of deploy-ports.ts, VERBATIM, with no behaviour change. The file is 399 lines and step 3 adds three verbs to it, so it crosses the 400-line hard split point; the seam is clean because :1-233 is production runners and :234-end is the test double. Move `ContainerState` (:234), `DockerDoubleOptions` (:236), `DOUBLE_IMAGE_COMMAND` (:258), the `ok`/`failed` helpers (:259-261), `DockerDouble` (:263) and `createDockerDouble` (:289) into a new apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-docker-double.ts, with the tracked `export * from "./deploy-docker-double.ts";` bridge every module in this directory has. THIS IS THE CRUX AND IT IS WHY THE ROW FITS: TWENTY files import those symbols from `deploy-ports.js` — daemon-command-async-entries.test.ts, eight deploy-*.test.ts, four rollback-*, three migrate-down-*, affordance-deployment-goals.test.ts, migrate-down-test-fixtures.ts, fake-docker-dependencies.ts and platform-pipeline-harness.ts. deploy-ports.ts MUST re-export all of them so not one of those twenty is edited. Assert it: an arm that the re-exported symbol set from deploy-ports.js is exactly the set the new module exports, so a future symbol added to the double and forgotten on the re-export is caught rather than discovered by a broken importer. AVOID A RUNTIME CYCLE: the double's `transfer` calls `dockerSaveArgv` and `sshDockerLoadArgv`, which live in deploy-ports.ts. Pass them into the double's factory rather than importing them back at runtime, and keep any back-import type-only. VERIFY THE MOVE AT THE ORIGIN, not the destination: `grep -Fxq` each deleted line against the new file so a "verbatim move" that silently reformatted or dropped a line is caught. `DOUBLE_IMAGE_COMMAND`'s exact bytes are pinned at deploy-candidate-environment.test.ts:129 — they must not move.

Teach the double `create`, `cp` and `start`, in the moved deploy-docker-double.ts. Today `dispatch` handles `run` by reading the `--name` VALUE (never the trailing argv, which is the image tag) and setting the container STARTING. Model create-then-start with the same key: `create` registers the name in a not-yet-running state, `start` moves it to STARTING, and `cp` is accepted only for a name that exists. The existing `run` path stays exactly as it is — this row wires nothing, so every current arm must keep passing untouched. Arms, each asserting the specific outcome and not merely that something happened: a container that was CREATED but never STARTED does not report itself running through `healthOf`/`inspect`; `cp` to an ABSENT container FAILS rather than succeeding silently, because a silent success is what would let a wired deploy start a candidate with no environment and blame the health probe; `cp` carries its payload on the `stdin` argument the dispatch already receives, and the double records it so a later row can assert no value reached an argv. Put these arms in deploy-candidate-environment.test.ts, which already imports `createDockerDouble` and `DOUBLE_IMAGE_COMMAND`, rather than opening a tenth file.

The USTAR encoder, in a new apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.ts plus its tracked `.js` bridge. It lives in its own module because deploy-candidate-environment.ts is already 217 lines against a 250-line target. Encode a single-file archive from the already-encoded environment text: 512-byte header, name, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime, the checksum computed over the header with the checksum field spaces-filled, typeflag, the `ustar\000` magic and version, then the data padded to a 512 multiple, then two zero blocks. THE uid AND gid FIELDS ARE NOT DECORATION — they carry the values step 1 measured for the image's app user, and getting them wrong produces a file the app cannot read. Include the directory entries the destination path needs if step 1 showed `docker cp` will not create them. Mode stays owner-only. The runner's stdin is a STRING, so the encoder must emit something that survives a UTF-8 round trip: headers are ASCII, but a variable VALUE is arbitrary text, so verify the byte length written into the size field is the UTF-8 byte length and not the JavaScript string length — a multi-byte character silently truncates the payload otherwise, and tar reports no error for a short read it was told to expect. Keep the module under 250 lines.

Archive arms, in a new deploy-candidate-archive.test.ts. VERIFY AGAINST A REAL READER, NOT AGAINST YOUR OWN DECODER — an encoder and a matching decoder agree on a wrong format all day. `bsdtar 3.8.8` is on this host: pipe the archive through `tar -tf -` and `tar -xOf -` and assert the exact path listing and the exact payload bytes come back, both exiting 0. Then assert the properties a reader cannot see: the header checksum validates against a recomputed checksum, the two trailing zero blocks are present, the total length is a multiple of 512, and the uid/gid fields carry the measured values. THE SECRECY ARM: the variable VALUE must appear in the DATA block and in NO header field — sweep the header bytes for it explicitly, because a long name or a mis-sized field is exactly how a value would bleed into a header. Cover a value containing a newline, a UTF-8 multi-byte character, a very long value, and a name at the USTAR 100-byte path limit; assert the refusal for anything that cannot be represented rather than silently truncating. Finally do the end-to-end read-back through Docker from step 1 as a committed arm where the environment allows it, so the encoder is proven against the consumer that actually matters.

The argv builders, in deploy-candidate-environment.ts. Add `createCandidateArgv`, `copyEnvironmentArgv` and `startCandidateArgv` alongside the existing `runCandidateArgv`, which is NOT touched. `createCandidateArgv` mirrors what `runCandidateArgv` builds today with `create` in place of `run --detach`, keeping the mount-null and mount-present shapes and the `--entrypoint` plus loader plus restored image argv that the module's header explains. `copyEnvironmentArgv` names the container and the destination path step 1 measured, with the archive-preserving flag if that probe required one — and NO value in any token, since the payload rides on stdin. `startCandidateArgv` is the container name alone. DoD 1 REQUIRES A BASELINE THAT CANNOT DRIFT: pin `runCandidateArgv` with an exact `toEqual` on BOTH its arms to the same bytes it produces at HEAD today, so the successor row's migration starts from something proven rather than from whatever this row left behind. The existing exact arms at :88-107 and the remote-refusal arms at :146-154 must pass UNCHANGED — if either needs an edit, something in this row reached past its scope and that is a stop-and-report, not an edit. Keep the file under 250 lines; the encoder is in its own module for exactly this reason.

Teach the control-room fake the new verbs, in tests/e2e/control-room/fake-docker-dependencies.ts:42. It seeds a candidate's health script keyed on `args[0] === "run"` and the `--name` value; a candidate started by create-then-start would get no health script at all and read as permanently unhealthy. Seed on create-or-start as well, with NO behaviour change for the `run` path — assert both: a run-started candidate gets the same script it gets today, and a create-then-start candidate gets one too. Seed once per container, not once per matching call, so create followed by start does not reset a script the arm is midway through consuming.

VERIFICATION, the NOTHING-IS-WIRED proof, and adversarial review. DoD 5 is the one a reviewer checks first: `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` must be EMPTY at completion, `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` must still exist with `resolveCandidateMount` still returning it for `sshTarget !== null`, and every pre-existing arm pinning the `run` verb must pass WITHOUT having been edited — name them in the record (deploy-build-authority.test.ts:31, deploy-journey.test.ts:660, deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:330, deploy-rollback.test.ts:111/:125/:142/:183, deploy-service.test.ts:159-162/:552/:779/:812/:850) as evidence the baseline was not disturbed. That is what lets the consumer row migrate them deliberately instead of discovering them broken. Legs, standalone and in the FOREGROUND, no pipes and no `;` chains: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Quote each command, exit code and `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line is UNVERIFIED, and `pnpm --filter` exits 0 printing "No projects matched the filters" on a bad package name. The count must RISE against the producer's 598 files / 10702 tests baseline, since this row adds a test file. Apply the path-attributed baseline for any repo-wide red: failing paths at merge-base versus HEAD, delta intersected with this row's nine owned paths must be EMPTY, foreign red quoted verbatim. THEN READ THE DIFF AS AN ATTACKER: is the re-export set from deploy-ports genuinely complete, or does a `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` pass only because the twenty importers use a subset today? Did the move introduce a runtime import cycle — check by importing deploy-docker-double.js first in a scratch script. Can `cp` to an absent container be made to look like success? Does the encoder mis-size a multi-byte value? Verify the failure arms by mutating the production surface and confirming each goes RED; prefer a process-local transform, and if you mutate on disk do it with no full-suite lease held, backing each path out of tree to `%TEMP%/moe-task-60f851fa3e-<basename>-<workerId>` — the task id in the path is mandatory because seat ids are reused across relaunches — hashing the LIVE file at window-open and proving the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. `git diff` is not a restore proof for the four new untracked files. Report all nine touched paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

Source matches the description: DockerRunner/SshRunner stdin?:string; runProcess writes string stdin; new builders/archive absent; candidate env=217 lines, ports=399, fake provider=120. IMPORTANT FILE CAP: move double implementation (:234-end) into deploy-docker-double.ts + .js, retain ports public createDockerDouble wrapper/types/value re-exports, pass existing save/load builders to internal factory and keep back-imports type-only to avoid a runtime cycle. Full planned roster can stay at 10 files including the archive .js bridge and new archive/fake tests. No runtime command roster/digest changes.

IMPORTANT PRIVILEGE DETAIL NOT IN DESCRIPTION: deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:91 emits USER node. Default `docker cp` gives copied files root ownership; a mode-0600 root-owned env would successfully copy but fail when the real app user reads it. Official docs: https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/cp/ (stdin tar extracts into an existing DIRECTORY; -a preserves source uid/gid). Current official Node alpine recipe creates node UID/GID 1000, but that is a LEAD, not verification of the pinned node:24.16.0-alpine image. Real preflight must measure the pinned runtime's id -u/id -g and require successful owner-only read-back as USER node, not as root. Do NOT solve unreadability by USER root or world-readable permissions. Proposed fixed root-target archive includes directory entries and env payload; use archive-preserving cp if confirmed by that probe. The runner's existing string stdin is sufficient for ASCII USTAR headers plus UTF-8 text data; no port widening needed.

Docker is still DOWN: separate `docker version --format '{{json .Server.Version}}'` invocation failed to connect to dockerDesktopLinuxEngine (named pipe absent). Tar is available: bsdtar 3.8.8. A read-only in-memory prototype (not shipped evidence) round-tripped a 4096-byte archive through UTF-8 string stdin, real tar -tf - and tar -xOf - run/moe/env both exited 0, exact paths/payload matched, zero marker bytes in headers. The WORKER must verify its actual encoder on real tar AND Docker; prototype output cannot discharge DoD.

Double trap: healthOf currently consumes scripted health for any extant non-REMOVED container. New CREATED state must not advance through health scripting or become HEALTHY before start. Keep the legacy run path untouched; no unrelated STOPPED-model cleanup here. Fake provider seeds only on run; make seeding additive on create, with --name-index guard. Native-child test of actual fake provider + exported existing docker runner avoids reimplementing seeding and proves the deployment .js bridges. Runtime-generated sentinels/credentials only; boolean/code/count output only, never values.

Asked human in REPL to confirm additive builders/string archive/small double extraction and bring Docker up. No plan submitted until approach is confirmed. Actual isEpicFinal:true is a highest-order LEAF artifact; this row does not replace the scoped integration parents/whole-product proof named by epic architectureNotes.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS CAME FROM A PEER ARCHITECT AND I VERIFIED BOTH BEFORE BUILDING ON THEM. architect-978f68c6 measured this row twice and released it without submitting; comment-090db6b7c8d74fe49a90b053a9706571 holds the findings. planningNotes.risks: THE OWNERSHIP PROBE IS A GO/NO-GO, NOT A DETAIL. The app runs as `USER node`; `docker cp` defaults copied files to root. A 0600 root-owned env file copies with exit 0 and is unreadable by the only process that needs it, and the symptom is a 150-second health timeout with nothing pointing at the cause — the same class of silent failure the mount design was chosen to avoid. If step 1 cannot establish a readable owner-only delivery, report rather than shipping builders that produce an unusable container, and do NOT buy readability with root or a world-readable mode. UTF-8 SIZING is silent when wrong: the USTAR size field is BYTES, the runner's stdin is a JavaScript STRING, and a multi-byte character makes the string length smaller than the byte length — tar then reads exactly as many bytes as it was told and reports no error for the truncation. THE RE-EXPORT SET IS THE MOVE'S FAILURE MODE: typecheck passes if the twenty importers happen to use a subset of the moved symbols, so a forgotten re-export ships green and breaks the first consumer that reaches for the missing one. Assert set equality against the new module's exports rather than trusting the compiler. VERIFY THE MOVE AT THE ORIGIN with `grep -Fxq` per deleted line — a reformatting "verbatim move" reads clean in review and changes pinned bytes, and `DOUBLE_IMAGE_COMMAND` is pinned exactly. RUNTIME CYCLE: deploy-ports imports the double and the double needs two argv builders from deploy-ports; a runtime back-import makes module initialisation order load-bearing, which typecheck will not catch. Prove it by importing the new module first in a scratch script. THE SCOPE FENCE IS THE OTHER HALF OF THIS ROW'S VALUE: if any pre-existing `run`-verb arm needs editing, something reached past scope — stop and report rather than editing, because those arms are the consumer row's migration baseline and five of them are negative assertions that would go silently vacuous. DoD 5's empty `git diff` on deploy-service.ts is the mechanical check. TEARDOWN: the ownership probe creates a real container and image; remove both on every exit path including the failure ones — epic rail 4 makes a leaked container inadmissible for every later gate on this board. `git diff` is blind to the four new untracked files, so it is not a restore proof for them during the mutation drills.
